Exam Date & Time: 26-Apr-2023 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIRST SEMESTER B.TECH. (MAKEUP) EXAMINATIONS - APRIL 2023  
  SUBJECT: PHY-1071 / PHY -1051 - ENGINEERING PHYSICS  
  (REGULARS - LATE ADMISSION BATCH)  
  Engineering Physics [PHY-1071]  
Marks: 50                                                                               Duration: 180 mins.  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
1A)          Obtain an expression for the radius of mth order bright ring in the case of Newton's  
  rings.                                                                                    (5)  
  
1B)           A helium-neon laser having a wavelength of 633 nm delivers 2.00 × 1018 photon/s. (i)  
  What is the energy of a photon in eV? (ii) If the beam shines perpendicularly onto a          (3)  
  perfectly reflecting surface, what force does it exert on the surface?  
  
1C)           The quantum number n of a particle of mass m confined to a one-dimensional "box" of  
  length L, when its momentum is 4h/L is 4. Is the above statement true /false? Justify.        (2)  
  
2A)           With necessary diagram, derive an expression for angle of acceptance and numerical  
  aperture for an optical fibre with refractive index of the material of the core n1 and  
  (5)  
  cladding n2 placed in a surrounding medium of refractive index n0.  
  
2B)           15.0 mW Helium-Neon laser emits a beam of circular cross section with a diameter of  
  2.00 mm. (i) Find the maximum electric field in the beam. (ii) What total energy is           (3)  
  contained in a 1.00 m length of the beam?  
  
2C)           The particle like an electron in an infinite potential well, can be at rest with its energy  
  E=0. State True or False and justify your answer.                                             (2)  
  
3A)           Derive the Compton shift equation for electromagnetic radiation like x-rays interacting  
  with a free or a nearly free electron.                                                        (5)  
  
3B)           Electrons are ejected from a metallic surface with speeds of up to 4.60 × 105 m/s when  
  light with a wavelength of 625 nm is used. (i) What is the work function of the surface? (3)  
  (ii) What is the cut-off frequency for this surface?  
  
3C)           In the photoelectric effect, explain why the stopping potential depends on the frequency  
  of light but not on the intensity.                                                       (2)  
  
4A)           Sketch schematically the plots of Fermi-Dirac distribution function for zero kelvin and  
  for temperature above zero kelvin. Derive an expression for density-of-states.                (5)  
  
4B)           Explain briefly the BCS theory of superconductivity in metals. Why all conductors are  
  not superconductors?                                                                          (3)  
  
4C)           For copper at 300 K, calculate the probability that a state with an energy equal to 99.0% (2)  
  of the Fermi energy is occupied. Fermi energy of copper is 7.05 eV. Mass of an electron

$$is 9.1x10-31 Kg ; speed of light in vacuum = 3x108 m/s; Planck's constant=6.63x10-34$$  
  $$Js; Avagadro number = 6.023x1023 / mol; Boltzmann constant=1.38x10-23 J/K.$$  
  
5A)             Derive an expression for density-of-states function for a metal.  
  (5)  
  
5B)             Taking the effective force constant of a vibrating HCl molecule as k = 480 N/m, find the  
  energy difference between the ground state and the first excited vibrational energy level. (3)  
  
5C)             Explain the concept of quantum confinement.  
  (2)  
  
  
-----End-----
